s1.syndrome_frame: Painless mass on the frontal bone with a 2-month history and associated radiographic findings
salient_findings: Painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
Lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance on CT
Lobulated frontal-bone mass with avid enhancement on MRI
key_facts: 50-year-old man
2-month history of a painless mass
Mass located on the right side of the frontal bone
Mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
Mass was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Neurologic examination was unremarkable
Plain radiography showed a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion
CT showed cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables
MRI showed a lobulated mass that was hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the skull
per_call: Solitary fibrous tumor of the skull

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Soap-bubble appearance on radiography and lytic lesion with cortical destruction on CT are characteristic of giant cell tumor

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed radiolucent lesion with a soap-bubble appearance on radiography is consistent with hemangioma of bone

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless mass on the frontal bone with a well-circumscribed radiolucent lesion on radiography could be an osteoma

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with cortical destruction on CT and a lobulated mass on MRI could be consistent with fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance on radiography and fluid-fluid levels on MRI could be an aneurysmal bone cyst

raw.rationale: The soap-bubble appearance on CT and the presence of a well-circumscribed, soft, and non-tender mass are characteristic of hemangioma of bone.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are typically more aggressive and have a higher recurrence rate, which does not match the patient's 2-month history of a painless mass.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are usually small, bony growths that do not typically present as a large, soft, and non-tender mass.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often presents with a ground-glass appearance on radiography, which is not consistent with the soap-bubble appearance described in the case.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are typically more expansile and have a fluid-fluid level on MRI, which is not mentioned in the case description.
